subject.title: RFC 0024: Localization Runtime and Product Coverage

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor RFC 0024 as the product-wide localization contract now, or first narrow it to an approved foundation that defers Gateway, channel, plugin, and release-policy commitments?
rationale: The branch is a detailed design proposal, but its requested decisions create cross-owner compatibility and product-policy commitments that cannot be resolved mechanically from repository policy or source evidence.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowed foundation
options.body: Accept the locale registry and internal rendering-kernel direction while deferring external Gateway, channel, plugin, and release-gate contracts to owner-approved follow-up RFCs or issues.

options.title: Sponsor the full contract
options.body: Assign owners to approve the listed API, recipient-locale, metadata, and release-gate commitments before changing the RFC from draft to accepted.

options.title: Keep it exploratory
options.body: Retain the RFC as a draft reference until maintainer-discussion produces consensus and an accepted implementation issue.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrowed foundation
recommendation.body: Accept the locale registry and internal rendering-kernel direction while deferring external Gateway, channel, plugin, and release-gate contracts to owner-approved follow-up RFCs or issues.

likelyOwner.reason: The proposal author is actively coordinating the documented implementation stack and can incorporate the sponsoring owners' decisions.
